nodes.norm_label: contract general rules (meters, internal coords, absolute z, ids as text)
nodes.rationale: Meters via 0.3048 conversion; internal project coordinates not shared; absolute Z so the app decides cuts per level (double-height walls appear on both levels); ids as strings to fit Revit 2024+ 64-bit ids and avoid collisions across linked models.

nodes.label: Inter-level building graph and routing
nodes.rationale: Hop costs in walked meters: stair/escalator 1.85x rise, ramp 12x rise, elevator 15 m wait + rise; connectors inferred from stacked stair/elevator rooms when absent; per-level scores unchanged.

nodes.label: Vegetation model (canopy, trunk blocks, shrubs)
nodes.rationale: Under a tree canopy one can walk and see, so only the trunk (6% of canopy radius, 0.12-0.30 m) blocks; shrubs or plants under 2.5 m block like any obstacle; tree belongs only to its planted level.

nodes.label: Python 2.7/3 compatibility rules
nodes.rationale: No f-strings, annotations, nonlocal or bare super(); utf-8 coding header; ElementId.Value not IntegerValue (removed in 2026+), sa_revit.common.id_value uses it only as fallback.

nodes.label: Restart Revit after lib/ changes
nodes.rationale: pyRevit keeps imported modules for the session; Reload only rereads button scripts and ribbon.

nodes.rationale: Elevators/escalators modeled in other categories recognized by name keywords; still exported as obstacles; model as one piece per shaft, not per floor.

nodes.label: Rainbow Conic-Gradient Ring Brand Identity
nodes.rationale: All pyRevit button icons reuse the app's rainbow conic-gradient ring (purple-pink-orange-green-blue) with a center glyph, so the Revit ribbon carries the same brand mark as the web app; dark variants use a light grey glyph for contrast on dark Revit themes.

nodes.label: Light/Dark Icon Theme Variants (pyRevit)
nodes.rationale: pyRevit picks icon.dark.png when Revit uses a dark UI theme; the glyph switches from near-black (light theme) to light grey (dark theme) while the ring stays identical.
